newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks down on profit-taking, Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks down on profit-taking, Wall Street.

text.p: Mexican stocks reversed short-lived initial gains to stand down in early trade on Wednesday due to what traders said was light profit-taking triggered by a downward Dow Jones.
"It opened up, but that was just follow-through on a couple of stocks that swayed a thin-volume market. It had every reason to go down," a desk trader said.
The leading IPC share index was down 11.96 points, or 0.27 percent, at 4,391.49.
"Most ADRs are down, Cetes rates went up, profit-taking was inevitable, but dealing is slow," a floor trader said.
The IPC rose as high as 4,407.58 points in the opening minutes of trade. Trading volume was light at 3.4 million shares.

Banco de Mxico assigned bellwether 28-day Cetes at 20.90 percent at Tuesday night's primary auction, an increase of 86 basis points over last week. Money market traders surveyed by Reuters had predicted a rise of 46 basis points.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average was meanwhile down 39.13 points at 7,718.93 points.
Dealers said financial stocks and cement maker Cemex weighed most on the market.
Mexico's two biggest financial groups, Bancomer and Banacci, led the decline after outperforming even the bourse's record-breaking breaking gains this month.
Bancomer B shares were off 1 centavo to 3.88 pesos, while Banacci B shares had shed 40 centavos to 20.95 pesos. Cemex had meanwhile fallen 15 centavos to 34.00 pesos.
Market heavyweight Telmex was off 4 centavos at 18.96 pesos, under the influence of its ADRs, off 1/16 to 47-3/4.

Dealers noted building company ICA was one of the few Mexican ADRs to buck the downtrend on Wall Street, and had gained 1/8 to 15-7/8 on favorable market reaction to Tuesday's news of a $1 billion package announced by the Mexican government to refinance highway concessions.
On the broad market, of 45 stocks traded in total, decliners outweighed gainers 23 to seven.
The Dow Jones meanwhile closed down 68.08 points at 7,689.98.
Dealers added the late downward trend was not due to a sell-off.
"Basically it was the Dow," a floor trader said. "Investors didn't bail out, they just took profits where they could. The market slid on moderate dealing."
"There was no overall message from the market. You had laggards, like financials, that gained, some profit-taking on outperformers, like Elektra, and some repositioning," Ruiz said.
Dealers said trade may also have been swayed by an opinion poll indicating the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) could lose its majority in the lower house for the first time since 1929.
Most earlier opinion polls had suggested the PRI could attain the minimum 42 percent needed for it to hang onto a majority in the lower house.
On the broad market, 118 stocks changed hands, of which sliders outpaced gainers by 46 to 42.
(( -- Martin Roberts, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-7907))
